function: Over-the-air aggregation of FL gradients: joint receive and transmit beamforming and MF-RIS coefficients minimizing the aggregation MSE; designed by classical optimization, not learned (pp. 5, 8).
system: BS with 4 antennas, 4 users with 2 antennas each, one MF-RIS with 36 elements (reflecting, refracting and amplifying), uplink at 3.5 GHz (p. 11).
method: Federated learning of a CNN on MNIST with AirComp aggregation; beamforming and MF-RIS designed by non-learned alternating optimization (SDR, DC programming) (pp. 8-13).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rician MF-RIS-aided channels, Rayleigh direct channel, path-loss exponents 3, 2.2, 3.8, statistical CSI error and channel aging; MNIST for the FL task (pp. 11, 13).
test_conditions: FL on MNIST split among 4 users, 50 rounds, test accuracy; MSE swept over power factor, user speed, CSI uncertainty, antennas, RIS elements; no unseen-condition test (pp. 11-14).
baselines: Own variants (Active RIS, STAR-RIS, SF-RIS as constrained cases of the design), random MF-RIS coefficients, noise-free FL; no earlier published aggregation design run (pp. 11-13).
metrics: MSE of gradient aggregation; test accuracy and training loss of the FL model over communication rounds; convergence of the algorithm (pp. 11-14).
complexity: Worst-case complexity O(T_out(1 + T1 K L^4.5 log(1/e1) + T2 N^4.5 log(1/e2))) and space complexity O(M + K L^2 + N^2) for the design (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 11: "We consider a Rician fading model for the MF-RIS-aided channels". Rayleigh for the direct channel and path-loss exponents from [37]; own simulator, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channels.
q2_support: p. 13: "Fig. 6 depicts MSEs in terms of varying". The experiments are sweeps of the MSE and MNIST runs under the one simulated setup; no model trained in one condition is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 11: "we consider the commonly used benchmark schemes as follows". Active RIS, STAR-RIS and SF-RIS are set by constraints on the same design (A_R = I_N, beta_max = 1), plus random coefficients (p. 13, Fig. 5b); no earlier published AirFL aggregation design is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "the overall computational complexity of the proposed algorithm is". Eq. (61) gives O(T_out(1 + T1 K L^4.5 log(1/e1) + T2 N^4.5 log(1/e2))), and the space complexity is O(M + K L^2 + N^2).
q5_support: p. 13: "using the widely adopted MNIST dataset". MNIST is a public dataset of the learning task only; channels come from the own simulator; no code or data link is given.
notes: Included: in over-the-air FL the learned element is the FL model (CNN on MNIST, p. 13), so no_learning does not apply even though the beamforming and MF-RIS design is classical alternating optimization (SDR with DC programming, pp. 8-11). Area 7 because the problem is the aggregation MSE itself. The Active, STAR and SF-RIS benchmarks are variants of the paper's own design, and the random case is its own heuristic, so q3 is 0.
